summary: This chunk adds three new files for an eval iteration of the adversarial-review-2 skill. benchmark.md reports pass rate, time, and token deltas between with-skill and without-skill runs, with a caveat that results come from a single run per eval. eval_metadata.json defines a red-team eval prompt asking the skill to review a checkout session-cache design with severities and a retest mechanism, listing nine required findings/behaviors. session-cache-design.md is the target design doc itself: a Redis session-pricing cache with TTL, KEYS-based invalidation, and sizing that consumes all free memory on a shared cluster.

claims.text: With-skill pass rate is 100% ± 0%, without-skill is 67% ± 0%, delta +0.33
With-skill time is 106.4s ± 16.4s, without-skill is 22.9s ± 8.2s, delta +83.5s
With-skill tokens are 62781 ± 5612, without-skill are 36016 ± 2879, delta +26765
The benchmark is one run per eval per arm across 2 evals, so the ± figure is a spread across evals, not run-to-run variance, and each delta should be treated as a single-draw observation
The eval expects the report to flag KEYS-based invalidation on the shared Redis cluster and rank it at or above conditional findings that depend on unverified facts
The eval expects the report to flag sizing math of 200k sessions x 40KB = 8GB, equal to all free memory on the shared cluster
The eval expects the report to flag a wrong/stale price window from TTL or invalidation gaps
The design caches per-session pricing (catalog prices, promos, tax rates) in a Redis hash session:{id}:pricing with a 30-minute TTL, keyed only by session ID
Invalidation on promo change is done by a consumer running KEYS session:*:pricing then DEL
Sizing is ~40KB per session hash at ~200k active sessions peak, against an existing cluster with 8GB free
On any cache error the design falls through to the three downstream calls, with no circuit breaker because fallthrough is the current behavior
The Redis cluster in this design also serves rate limiting and feature flags

risks.note: Invalidation relies on a KEYS scan across the shared cluster, which blocks Redis during the scan; the doc presents this as adequate without addressing the impact on the co-located rate-limiting and feature-flag traffic.

40KB x 200k sessions = 8GB is presented as fitting exactly the cluster's free memory, leaving no headroom for growth, overhead, or the cache's own metadata, but no margin or eviction policy is discussed.

Cache key is session ID only, and the only stated invalidation trigger is a promo_changed event; a tax-rate change is not named as an invalidation trigger, so a stale tax rate could be served for up to the 30-minute TTL.

least_confident: Whether the benchmark's single-run-per-eval caveat means the reported pass-rate and token deltas should be read as directionally suggestive only, since the chunk gives no indication of statistical significance.
